finding: §3.3 groups "the environment" with .tp/config.json and a task override as a stored layer that yields a validation error (exit 1) when it holds an invalid winning review_converge_on value, justifying exit 1 with "the invocation itself is correct and the fault is the stored value." But an env var (e.g. TP_REVIEW_CONVERGE_ON=bad tp review --status) is supplied at the invocation, like a CLI flag — which §3.3 classifies as a usage error (exit 2). By §3.3's own stated rationale the env value is part of the (now incorrect) invocation, so it points to exit 2, contradicting the exit-1 classification. Test 17 compounds the gap: it pins exit 2 for the two `set` commands and exit 1 only for "a hand-edited stored layer" (naturally read as an on-disk file, not a shell env var), leaving the invalid-env case unpinned. Two engineers would write contradictory exit-code assertions for an invalid env-provided value: one exit 1 (per §3.3's layer list), one exit 2 (per §3.3's rationale and the CLI-usage parallel).

resolved.evidence: Accepted per the no-critical convergence policy (spec 0.31.0 §3-4, CLAUDE.md): no critical/high finding across 22 review rounds. This residual medium is an exit-code-classification judgment for the rare invalid-env review_converge_on edge case (env is invocation-time yet grouped with stored layers); either exit 1 or exit 2 is defensible, and core validation is specified. Acceptance-level detail deferrable to implementation/patch; recorded in .tp-review for a future maintainer.

suggestion: State the invalid-env exit code explicitly and reconcile it with the rationale: either (a) keep env at exit 1 and drop/replace the "invocation itself is correct" rationale (since env is an invocation input) with one that covers env, or (b) move env to exit 2 alongside CLI/flag arguments, leaving exit 1 only for on-disk stored layers (.tp/config.json, task override). Add a Test 17 clause asserting the chosen exit code for an invalid env-provided winning value so it is verifiable.
